notes.characters: mobile/r04-pond and mobile/r08-barn show appealing expressive gators with rounded painted volume and recognizable sleeping poses. mobile/r10-boss adds an angry scarred face, but the regular cast repeats very similar green silhouettes. Bandit's soft fur and mostly rear-facing silhouette in mobile/r11-hop feel less graphically defined than the glossy gators. Below the 7 consistency/distinction anchor.
notes.environment: desktop/r01-title has a rich cohesive pond, boardwalk, vegetation and spring backdrop. Gameplay in mobile/r04-pond and mobile/r08-barn instead reads as repeated straight texture strips; the barn is largely straw alternating with the same bright outdoor water. The gap between composed title art and tiled gameplay holds this close to the coherent-but-flat anchor.
notes.depth: mobile/r04-pond provides waterline ripples and mobile/r11-hop has cast shadows, so volume is present. However, land-gator shadows stretch as hard flat ovals, concrete edges are uniform straight bands, and mobile/r09-night uses darkening plus flat dashed light ellipses rather than integrated illumination. mobile/r08-barn lacks a distinctive interior light treatment. Below the clear cohesive depth expected at 7.
notes.readability: mobile/r04-pond and mobile/r11-hop have recognizable open jaws, conspicuous warning triangles and contrasting snacks. However, caustics compete with silhouettes, triangles can cover gator bodies rather than isolate the dangerous head, and the HUD masks upper lanes. mobile/r10-boss crops much of the boss at the left edge. Readable with attention, short of instant phone readability.
notes.ui: desktop/r01-title and mobile/r13-results (contact sheet mobile-02) show a deliberate cream/yellow palette, strong button outlines and legible hierarchy. mobile/r04-pond shows oversized floating HUD panels covering active scenery; mobile/r02-map and mobile/r14-help in the sheets show content extending beyond the visible panel area without an obvious visible scroll cue. Designed, but not yet at the 7 anchor throughout.
notes.juice: mobile/r11-hop and desktop/r11-hop show a raised Bandit pose, carried snacks and a separated shadow; mobile/r04-pond shows open jaws and waterline marks. These stills communicate states but little energetic hop feedback: no visible takeoff puff, trajectory accent or landing burst. mobile/r09-night's simple glow blobs and dashed ellipses reinforce the utilitarian FX treatment. Motion timing cannot be judged from these stills.
notes.mobile: mobile/r08-barn and mobile/r11-hop fill portrait height with large readable sprites and a substantial lure target. mobile/r04-pond loses upper-lane visibility behind HUD panels, and mobile/r10-boss reveals only part of the boss silhouette at the left edge. The tall framing works structurally but compromises encounter visibility and interface clearance.
notes.authenticity: desktop/r01-title explicitly names Hot Springs and states non-affiliation, with a steaming stone spring, gator ponds and boardwalks; no recognizable real logo is visible there. mobile/r08-barn and mobile/r10-boss show generic striped playfields with little farm infrastructure or local identity. The title carries most of the setting; gameplay needs more visual specificity to reach 6.5. No commercial mascot resemblance observed in the viewed captures.

gaps.issue: Large top HUD panels obscure gators, items and a warning in the upper playfield.
gaps.fix: Reserve a dedicated top HUD safe area and start playable lane rendering below it; compress counters into one compact strip.

gaps.issue: The boss is mostly outside the left portrait boundary, hiding its body and weakening the encounter silhouette.
gaps.fix: Clamp the boss reveal position to the portrait camera bounds and frame its full head and enough body to distinguish its scale before it traverses the edge.

gaps.issue: The barn reads as straw strips beside tropical-bright water, with no visible enclosure or barn structure.
gaps.fix: Add painted timber framing and trough walls at lane margins, a roof-shadow band and warm lamp pools; recolor water toward muted interior reflections.

gaps.issue: High-frequency white water caustics compete with gator contours and waterline marks.
gaps.fix: Reduce caustic contrast and detail beneath traversal lanes, keeping the strongest highlights near banks and using a darker local water halo under gators.

gaps.issue: Dashed elliptical light pools and triangular beams look like flat overlays rather than light interacting with painted surfaces.
gaps.fix: Feather pool edges, remove decorative dashes unless mechanically necessary, and apply the light mask to terrain and sprites together with localized warm highlights.

gaps.issue: Land gators cast long hard oval shadows that read as detached flat shapes.
gaps.fix: Use a tight dark contact shadow under feet and belly plus a softer lower-opacity directional shadow aligned to the scene light.

gaps.issue: Gameplay is dominated by repeated horizontal texture strips and uniform straight concrete borders, unlike the composed title scene.
gaps.fix: Paint varied bank-edge segments, occasional inset rocks and reeds, and foreground edge occluders while preserving clear traversal cells.

gaps.issue: The hop pose has little visible energetic feedback beyond elevation and a small oval shadow.
gaps.fix: Add a short painted takeoff dust puff and trailing motion strokes, with a squash landing pose and expanding contact ring on landing.

gaps.issue: Warning triangles sit over gator backs or on nearby terrain without precisely marking the dangerous jaw area.
gaps.fix: Anchor warnings above the biting head with a short pointer and highlight the threatened landing cell using a consistent warm outline.

gaps.issue: Regular gator kinds share similar green bodies; small tail stripes and mouth bands must carry much of their distinction under dark lighting.
gaps.fix: Give each kind a stronger silhouette cue and controlled accent color, preserving those accents through the night tint.

gaps.issue: The visible help panel ends mid-explanation near the bottom, with no obvious visible cue that more content follows.
gaps.fix: Add a persistent scroll indicator and bottom fade, and keep a close/back control fixed outside the scrolling text area.

gaps.issue: The gameplay setting contains little visual evidence of a managed gator farm or Hot Springs beyond the animals.
gaps.fix: Add original illustrated enclosure fixtures, feeding-platform railings and a small generic thermal-water feature at safe margins, without real branding.

gaps.issue: Bandit's small soft rear silhouette reveals little face or personality compared with the expressive gators.
gaps.fix: Use a slightly turned head in the hop pose, strengthen the ear and mask outline, and exaggerate paw spread so the raccoon reads clearly at gameplay scale.
